headline: Mechanistic models link tumor dynamics to therapy, drug tolerance, and preclinical design
label: Mechanistic Tumor Simulation Models
summary: Quantitative models now simulate tumor evolution under combination therapy and resistance, and assess the experimental designs used to test them.
synthesis: The three preprints share a coupling of tissue-scale tumor dynamics to treatment rather than a common formalism. The renal cell carcinoma study combines ODEs with stochastic modelling, coupled to pharmacokinetics, to simulate advanced RCC evolution and optimize bevacizumab plus atezolizumab combination therapy within a cancer-immunity cycle framework. The agent-based persister study couples population dynamics with epigenetic state inheritance across the cell cycle to represent drug-tolerant resistance in solid tumors. The acute leukaemia study fits exponential and logistic growth models to mouse time series and reports that they outperform a two-timepoint test at detecting simulated knockout effects, shifting emphasis toward evaluation of preclinical experimental design. What is new is the explicit linkage of mechanistic simulation to therapeutic decisions and to the design of the experiments that inform them.
